body:
#2035 (BUG-1470) APPROVED at 70a11d23b4. All four findings closed, and three
of the four fixes go past what I asked.

F1 CLOSED AT A BETTER SEAM THAN I NAMED. I asked for the advisor-authority
check the sibling sites apply. They put it AT THE FLIP rather than at target
selection — which also covers an explicit `--status` override, a side door
that would have stayed open once the one I cited was closed. It refuses BEFORE
any side effect (no status write, no comment, no queue entry), and the paired
test asserts both halves: refused AND no queue entry left behind.

F2 FIXED BY DERIVATION, NOT BY EDITING THE SENTENCE I QUOTED. The nine-status
table was built by READING rework_target_for_mode and rework_smart_target.
They also found clap was REFLOWING the doc comment into unreadable prose,
added verbatim_doc_comment, and VERIFIED BY RENDERING `--help` rather than
assuming — fixing a pre-existing rendering defect on the command sequence
above it that nobody had reported.

F3 FIXED AND MUTATION-CHECKED. The pass-through arm is asserted, and they
confirmed the exact mutation I described — collapse the metadata-only block to
a constant — now FAILS. Both new guards were mutation-checked rather than
written and asserted.

F4 DISPOSED OF EXPLICITLY. Three specs filed, and I CONFIRMED THEY EXIST:
BUG-1564, TASK-1423, STORY-1429 — all Draft, children of EPIC-62, tagged
followup:BUG-1470. They split rather than held because each is a separate
surface or decision, and holding a tested fix to a LIVE AUTHORITY BYPASS
behind three unrelated surfaces is the worse trade. I agree.

THE PART I WANT TO NAME: THEY ANTICIPATED THE AUTO-BUMP HAZARD THEMSELVES.
The commit says merging completes BUG-1470 and would otherwise close four
acceptance criteria having satisfied one — and they filed the three specs
BECAUSE of that, before anyone raised it. That is the five-state predicate
being reasoned about by an implementer at write time rather than caught by a
reviewer at merge time, which is where it costs least.

ONE THING FOR YOUR TRAILER DECISION, recorded as a finding: a trailer naming
BUG-1470 auto-completes it with 1 of 4 criteria met. The other three are
tracked and will not be lost, so I think completing is defensible and I am NOT
objecting. But it is a choice, not a default — BUG-1470 is a BUG, not an EPIC,
so its status is not a rollup of those children, and a later reader checking
its four criteria will find one met and three elsewhere. If you keep the
trailer, the delegation should be visible ON BUG-1470, not only in the commit
message.

Board from this seat: 7 open, all reviewed at their current heads, nothing
awaiting me.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2035 approved - F1 closed at a BETTER seam (gate at the flip, covers --status override). And they anticipated the auto-bump hazard themselves, filing 3 specs before anyone raised it
